target_customer: Government contractors (GovCon firms) that bid on federal work
problem: Contractors spend two to four weeks per proposal on manual drafting or consultants, which caps how many bids they can submit; GovDash automates capture, proposals and post award work.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with a pilot offer for government contractors
product_category: AI proposal, capture and contract management software for GovCon

founders.name: Sean Doherty
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder on the YC page and as CEO in press; background not found in sources I opened.

founders.name: Timothy Goltser
education: Stony Brook University, computer science (alum per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him an engineer.

founders.name: Curtis Mason
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page; no background listed.

competitors.name: Govly
competitors.what: Public sector procurement network and opportunity tool for contractors
competitors.funding_then: A 3.6M USD seed in Aug 2021 appears on Dealroom only, unverified

competitors.name: Deltek GovWin
competitors.what: Legacy government market intelligence platform used for opportunity tracking
competitors.funding_then: Owned by Roper Technologies since Dec 2016 per a search summary

technical_complexity.rationale: In 2022 the product was workflow software for capture and proposals; the AI drafting layer and GCC High and CUI security later raised the bar. At founding mostly standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Becomes a system of record across capture, proposals and contracts with compliance features such as CUI handling and GCC High, which creates lock in; early on, proposal tools were copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquired or copied it in sources found; later AI entrants such as Vultron raised seed money after the batch.

market_need_then: US government spends over 650B USD per year on contracted work, nearly all through formal RFPs; proposals take two to four weeks each (Northzone and company sources).

identity.voice_and_tone: Insider GovCon voice, tagline: Build a next-generation GovCon company

branding.brand_signature: A GovCon community with events and podcasts hosted around the product
branding.community_and_virality: Company site describes a user community and events; CEO appears on GovCon podcasts; claims 10,000 plus GovCon professionals as users (company claim).

brand_strength.rationale: Name states what it does for the niche, TechCrunch covered the Series A, and community and events show brand investment; no evidence of mass virality.

outcome_analysis: GovDash raised a 10M Series A in April 2024 and a 30M Series B in January 2026, and now has about 56 people. The company claims 16x revenue growth over the past year and top 100 contractor customers. Generative AI made proposal drafting a strong wedge in a large, document heavy government market, and the company expanded into capture and contract management.
notes: Series A confirmed by the company blog, Fintech Global and Northzone; Series B by the company blog and SiliconANGLE. CB Insights lists a seed round dated 2022-04-18 with an unknown amount, not recorded as a round. Press says total funding was 12M after the Series A, implying about 2M earlier, a computation not stated, so not recorded. A search summary says the founders built an earlier app called Hang, unverified so not listed. Northzone page says founded 2023, a search says 2022, YC says 2021, unresolved. Competitor sources: Govly seed is aggregator only; Deltek ownership is from a search summary.
